## 2026-11-17 01:23 · The lead to the builder (Design lead for step 2.37 part 1, thing 3)

From the lead, one thing to add to lane 2.37, and it comes before the pictures of thing 3 because it may be a real fault in what a scorekeeper relies on. GitHub FAILED one commit of the build branch tonight (71eef18, a record-only commit on top of the Next.js 16.4.6 landing; the three commits after it passed) in `node tests/browser/scoring-screen-test.mjs --no-build`: "Scoring screen browser test: 3 problem(s)", among them "every tap opened its options and its play was counted on the tile: 100 opened, 99 counted" (the notes beside it: "every play was written to the device's store before the tile counted it (T-114): 99 plays timed; counted before written: []"; "an option's tap is painted on the tile within 100 ms, 95 times in 100: marked: 99 taps, median 42 ms, 95th in 100 50 ms, slowest 54 ms"). That run's machine was pathologically slow: the job took 67 minutes where it takes about 10. Read the failed job yourself: `node -e` with `fetch` to `https://api.github.com/repos/mrsaiyed/league-platform/actions/runs/43986010617/jobs` gives the job id, and `…/check-runs/<job id>/annotations` its notes (start the command with the env file, which sends Node's fetch through the proxy); read-only. FIND OUT WHICH IT IS, and do not guess: (A) THE PRODUCT CAN LOSE A TAP WHEN THE DEVICE IS SLOW: a tap on an option that opened is not recorded (the pad still settling, a handler not yet attached, a re-render swallowing the touch, a tap landing in a rest window meant for another button). The screen is for "a phone or a tablet that may be five years old" (DESIGN.md section 7): a lost play at a scorer's table is the worst thing this screen can do. If so it is a HIGH finding of your lane: fix it, with a test that makes the page slow on purpose (the browser's CPU throttling through the devtools protocol, 6 and 20 times slower) and proves 100 taps give 100 plays, at the short phone, in both faces. (B) THE TEST READS TOO EARLY on a starved machine (it counts the tile before the play it tapped has been drawn, or its tap is sent before the option is ready, where a person would simply see the option a moment later): make the check sturdy WITHOUT weakening it: it must still fail when a tap is truly lost (prove that by dropping one tap on purpose in a copy). Either way, run the speed part of the scoring-screen test with the CPU throttled and say what it shows; say in your report which of A and B it was, with the run that shows it; and keep every tap-to-paint time limit as it is (they passed on that slow run). Everything else in your brief stands.

THE POSSIBLE LOST TAP: IT IS (B), the test read the wrong sign; no tap was lost. GitHub's own run shows it: 100 opened, 99 marked, but "the store wrote once for each of the hundred plays" did NOT fail, so 100 plays were written. Cause: the watch timed a tap by a change of the tile's mark text, and a new "+2" over a "+2" still showing (the store answered late) writes no new text (`tile-marks.ts` writes only what differs). Reproduced here: the test as it stood, with the store answering 400 ms late, gave the same three failures with 100 plays recorded (10 marks seen of 100). Throttled runs at the short phone: 6x and 20x, with 0 and 500 taps waiting, own and wider letters: 100 taps, 100 plays, 200 points, 100 writes every time. Speed part throttled: 6x passes everything (95th 35 and 37 ms); 20x records all 100 and misses only the two paint limits (108 ms against 100). Fix: the watch looks for a new mark by text or by its fade's name; a late count is timed from its own tap; one new check counts plays and points by the game itself. With one tap swallowed on purpose in a copy it fails in five checks (99 plays, 198 points, 99 writes). Every time limit unchanged. Probes are in the lane's `.local/probe/` (git-ignored).

TAKEN FROM THE STANDARDS: Al-Hadi's question wording (score counts, can be reopened), "Final" with Reopen beside it, clock/period/Undo/Redo greyed, a tap on a player saying the game is final. First demo: a review step before finalizing, and the state said on the scoreboard. Not copied: the browser's own confirm box, a one-tap reopen with no question.
